mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals increased demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same period, it signals robust demand and labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both RSAFS and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% month-over-month and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter, it signals strong supply-side growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both INDPRO and GDPC1 meet the trigger conditions.
